producer_report.summary: Added `athena focus` and the urgent/high priority caps. `athena focus "<text>"` appends an `athena.focus/1` record at records/focus/<month>/<id>.json, holding the text, the git user.name and a counter `n`. The record with the highest `n` is the current focus. `athena focus` with no text prints it, and `athena status` shows a `focus` line (and a `focus` field in `--json`). `[priority_caps]` in athena.toml (urgent = 3, high = 10) is backed by a defaulted schema struct, reset in `reading_inputs` and skipped when serialized at its defaults, so reading digests do not move. `Plan::build_capped` caps each item's own priority, in memory only. Urgent excess drops to high and then counts in the high pass, whose excess drops to normal. Items a person gave a priority record are always kept at that tier, even when they alone pass the cap. The plan is then rebuilt from the capped priorities, and one `Demotion` is recorded per item whose final tier ended lower. `athena plan` prints one `demoted <id>: ...` line per demotion. `drain.rs` (not in the listed deliverables) was needed: `Drain::prepare` is the only production caller of the plan builder, and caps and person-set reach it only through a new defaulted `Steps::priority_caps`. The full `cargo test --locked` passed (exit 0), as did clippy with -D warnings, fmt and the policy scan.

open_issues: Departure from the plan: crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs was edited although the brief's deliverables do not list it. It is the only production caller of the plan builder, and caps and the person-set reach it only through the new defaulted `Steps::priority_caps`. Without it the caps would never govern `athena plan` or `drain`.

Open question for the owner, as in the plan: a person's priority record is never demoted, so 13 person-set urgent items would still all stay urgent. If the caps should bind person-set items too (oldest set demoted first), the reading must change.
An item pushed out of the high tier lands at normal, two tiers below urgent, with one merged `demoted` line showing its final from and to.
Raised prerequisites are not counted against a cap, so more than 3 items can be treated as urgent when a kept urgent item depends on others. The CHANGELOG says this.
I did not add a unit test for the missing git user.name error in `set_focus`: a global git identity on the machine would make it unreliable. The empty-text refusal is covered by a binary test.
mistakes: My first plan test expected the wrong plan order for an urgent item with a prerequisite, because the independent urgent item comes before the dependent in plan order. I rewrote the expectation after working it through, before running the tests.
The first focus commit lacked the Athena-Record trailer and the gate refused it; the binary tests caught it and I added the trailer.
learnings: A commit that adds a record outside a job needs an `Athena-Record: <canonical path>` trailer, or the gate refuses it; a bare commit_records message fails.

Request text with a path-like word (src/itemN.rs) and a `- ` bullet gives a complete plan entry before any reading: the goal is the first line, the rung is inferred Implementation from the touched path, and the acceptance is the bullet. `athena plan --budget 0` then plans it with no model call.
`tests/common::test_config()` embeds the repository's athena.toml, so it now carries `[priority_caps]`; a test changes a cap with `replacen("urgent = 3\n", ...)`, not by appending a second section.
The cargo tool refuses `tail`, pipes and reading /tmp, so a long foreground test run that passes 20 minutes goes to the background and is only seen through its completion notification.
An urgent item that depends on older prerequisites comes after them in the uncapped plan order, so a newer independent urgent item is earlier in 'plan order' than its dependent.
desires: A way to wait for a background test run, or to read its output file, from inside the working directory.
